record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: For which structurally defined classes of real symmetric matrices can copositivity be fully characterized? Here a real symmetric n x n matrix A is copositive if x^T A x >= 0 for every vector x in the nonnegative orthant R_+^n.

evidence.quote: For what other classes of matrices can copositivity be fully characterized?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A real symmetric n×n matrix A is called copositive if x^T A x ≥ 0 for every vector x in the nonnegative orthant R_+^n. Some structurally defined classes of real symmetric matrices admit complete characterizations of copositivity. For example, a symmetric matrix all of whose off-diagonal entries are nonpositive is copositive if and only if it is positive semidefinite; symmetric matrices with all entries nonnegative are automatically copositive; and tridiagonal or, more generally, acyclic (tree-structured) symmetric matrices admit known sign-pattern based criteria for copositivity.

Problem: Identify further structurally defined classes C of real symmetric n×n matrices (defined by sign patterns, graph patterns of nonzero off-diagonal entries, rank or nullity constraints, or other intrinsic structural conditions) for which copositivity within C can be fully characterized by explicit, verifiable conditions on the entries of A (rather than by a general membership test in the copositive cone, which is co-NP-complete). Provide such classes together with the characterizations, or prove obstructions to obtaining them for given candidate classes.
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys and problem lists on copositive and completely positive matrices continue to list the characterization of copositivity for broader structured classes (beyond matrices with nonpositive off-diagonal entries, small dimensions, or acyclic patterns) as open. General copositivity testing is known to be co-NP-complete, and recent work (e.g., Oberwolfach reports, copositive programming surveys, and 2020s arXiv contributions) extends partial results without producing a comprehensive characterization.

status_evidence.title: Copositive Programming – a Survey (Dür)
status_evidence.snippet: Testing copositivity is co-NP-complete; explicit characterizations are known only for restricted classes.
status_evidence.claim: No general characterization beyond restricted structured classes is known.

status_evidence.title: Oberwolfach Report No. 52/2017
status_evidence.snippet: Recent advances on extreme copositive matrices and structured cases are discussed but the general structural characterization remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues without resolving the general structural-class characterization.
